# Final Report: Anagram Analysis ## Summary of Investigation This investigation focused on identifying and documenting a specific anagram puzzle related to Shakespeare's Hamlet. Through systematic internet searches and website analysis, I successfully identified the solution and gathered comprehensive supporting documentation. --- ## FINAL ANSWER ### The Famous Shakespeare Line The anagram **"In one of the Bard's best thought-of tragedies, our insistent hero, Hamlet, queries on two fronts about how life turns rotten"** unscrambles to: **"To be or not to be: that is the question, whether tis nobler in the mind to suffer the slings and arrows of outrageous fortune."** This is the opening line of Hamlet's famous soliloquy from Act 3, Scene 1 of William Shakespeare's *Hamlet*. --- ## Detailed Supporting Information ### Creator and Significance **Creator:** Cory Calhoun, a renowned master anagrammist **What Makes This Anagram Exceptional:** 1. It uses exactly the same letters as the original Shakespeare quote 2. The anagram text itself cleverly summarizes the plot of Hamlet 3. It's considered one of the most impressive anagrams ever created due to its dual functionality - being both a perfect anagram and a meaningful description of the play ### Documentation and Sources This anagram is widely documented and celebrated across multiple platforms: **Primary Sources Found:** 1. **Braingle.com** (Brain Teaser #4624) - URL: https://www.braingle.com/brainteasers/4624/amazing-anagram.html - Listed as a language brain teaser puzzle - Includes hint: "BB or not BB" 2. **Mental Floss Magazine** (March 12, 2013) - URL: https://www.mentalfloss.com/article/49411/cory-calhoun-master-anagrammist - Featured article: "Cory Calhoun, Master Anagrammist" - Highlights this as Calhoun's "most famous anagram" - Includes video documentary "Ars Magna" from 2013 PBS Online Film Festival 3. **Internet Anagram Hall of Fame** - URL: http://www.chem.ucla.edu/~ltfang/humors/anagram.html - Listed among celebrated anagrams 4. **Additional References:** - Reddit (r/words) - December 2025 discussion - Shaksper.net archive (April 1998) - Various puzzle and wordplay forums - Facebook puzzle groups - Eileen's Lounge forum discussions ### Additional Context from Mental Floss Article The Mental Floss article revealed that: - Cory Calhoun is a natural anagrammist who can shuffle letters mentally - He has created numerous impressive anagrams including presidential names and other literary quotes - A documentary film titled "Ars Magna" (itself an anagram) was made about his anagramming achievements - The film was part of the 2013 PBS Online Film Festival ### Quote from Mental Floss: > "His most famous anagram takes the first few lines of a famous soliloquy from Hamlet and effectively summarizes the play using an anagram of those lines." --- ## Verification The anagram has been cross-verified across multiple independent sources spanning from 1998 to 2025, confirming its authenticity and widespread recognition in wordplay and puzzle communities. It is consistently attributed to Cory Calhoun and is celebrated as a masterpiece of anagrammatic art.
